heroHeadline: Day 662: Ex-Sinaloa Security Chief Mérida Sánchez First of 10 Indicted Officials to Surrender to US; Appears in SDNY Manhattan Court
heroSubtitle: 662 days of cartel civil war — May 15: Former Sinaloa Secretary of Public Security Gerardo Mérida Sánchez voluntarily surrendered in Arizona (May 11) and appeared in Manhattan SDNY federal court — the first of the 10 officials indicted April 29 to face US justice. He allegedly accepted $100,000/month from Los Chapitos to warn them of at least 10 upcoming law enforcement raids in 2023. His cooperation as a former state security chief holds major intelligence value for future Chapitos prosecutions. The remaining nine indicted officials — including Governor Rocha Moya and Culiacán Mayor Gámez Mendívil — remain in Mexico as the US-Mexico extradition standoff enters Day 17 with FGR maintaining the US evidence package is insufficient; El Mayo sentencing before EDNY Judge Cogan set July 20; La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops in Sinaloa; war toll ~2,425+ since Sep 9, 2024.
